page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics processing and substantial system memory. The hardware configuration features an Intel x86_64 processor with 12 shared vCPUs, derived from 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 8665.1 tokens per second with a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second with a medium 7B model. Text generation performance is also strong, reaching 32.35 tokens per second on the 7B model, which ranks in the top 25 percent. General compute and memory benchmarks fall within the average range, with a PassMark CPU score of 20085.48 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 21080.54. Memory read-only bandwidth for large uncached blocks is recorded at 102.38 GB/sec, while write bandwidth is 53.61 GB/sec.

The instance presents a balanced profile for memory-intensive and GPU-accelerated tasks, though the shared CPU allocation may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU compute-heavy workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dual NVIDIA Ampere GPUs and a generous 128 GB memory allocation provides high resource density for specialized workloads without the premium of dedicated bare-metal hardware. This server is highly suited for medium-scale LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, database operations, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
